memories.content: Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the prototype.
Cross-check whether evaluation tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether collected evidence aligns with design and operational decisions to be changed.
Verify at the end that user problems, design interventions, user studies, and expected contributions form a coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions are not linked to prototype functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if evaluation tasks do not produce representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practicality of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Cross-check at the end whether each research question, formative evaluation data, and design modification judgment are seamlessly connected.
Review whether the application conditions of proposed design principles and boundary cases of failure are presented together.
The user can have contributions reviewed only if prototype outcomes and the transferable design knowledge derived from them are separated.
The scope of observation in controlled formative evaluations does not include long-term adaptation and operational changes in real-world usage contexts.
Specify a single representative measure that will drive operational decisions to maintain, modify, or discontinue the deployed design.
The HCI review panel verifies whether operational decisions can be made based on the declared primary measure.
Establish decision thresholds indicating at what levels key metrics trigger maintaining, modifying, or discontinuing the design.
Evaluate whether reducing workload for one role creates new tasks for other roles through the proposed design changes.
Distinguish usability from organizational adoption intent as separate evaluation outcomes.
Implementation fidelity indicates whether planned features and operational procedures were delivered in the field according to intended specifications.
Initial evaluations and long-term operation do not share identical measurement conditions due to differences in system exposure duration and frequency of repeated use.

analysis.overview: Both frames connect evaluation evidence to consequential design and operational decisions. They differ mainly in emphasis: the reference stresses submission-time coherence, transferable knowledge, and evaluation boundaries, while the compared frame adds decision thresholds, organizational effects, adoption, and field-delivery measures.

relations.reason: The reference states alignment and review-validity requirements, while the compared frame specifies a primary measure, panel verification, and decision thresholds; these are complementary requirements for evidence-based decisions.
relations.summary: Representative measures and collected evidence should be aligned with evaluation tasks and capable of supporting explicit design or operational decisions.

relations.reason: The reference excludes long-term adaptation and real-world operational change from controlled formative observation, while the compared frame attributes nonidentical measurement conditions to exposure duration and repeated use; the evaluation horizon explains and preserves the distinction.
relations.summary: Controlled or initial evaluation and long-term field operation have different observational and measurement scopes.

relations.reason: These reference memories divide one overall coherence audit into its timing, focus, broad logical flow, and specific research-question-to-modification connections, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A focused submission-time review should verify coherent logical connections among user problems, research questions, interventions, formative evidence, design judgments, studies, and contributions.

relations.reason: The reference supplies both the cross-check and its review consequence as two parts of one underlying validity claim, which the compared frame does not address.
relations.summary: Research questions should be linked to the prototype’s core functions to sustain the validity of design interventions.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only requirement concerning the qualified scope of design principles.
relations.summary: Proposed design principles should present their application conditions together with failure boundary cases.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only condition for making the nature of contributions reviewable.
relations.summary: Prototype outcomes should be separated from the transferable design knowledge derived from them when presenting contributions for review.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim introduces an independent cross-role consequence of design changes.
relations.summary: Evaluation should determine whether workload reductions for one role create new tasks for other roles.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim establishes an independent distinction between interaction quality and organizational willingness to adopt.
relations.summary: Usability and organizational adoption intent should be evaluated as separate outcomes.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim defines implementation fidelity as an independent field-delivery outcome.
relations.summary: Field evaluation should assess whether planned features and operational procedures were delivered according to intended specifications.

reports.both: Both require representative evaluation evidence to support design and operational decisions.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds cross-role workload effects, separate usability and adoption outcomes, and implementation fidelity.
reports.differences: Controlled formative evaluation is distinguished from long-term operation, whose exposure, repeated use, adaptation, and operational conditions require preserving different measurement scope.
reports.reference_only: The reference adds submission-time coherence checks, prototype–research-question linkage, design-principle boundaries, and separation of prototype outcomes from transferable knowledge.
